Anybody here got good advice on how to stop smoking? I feel like I've tried everything

I was fortunate enough to have a healthy lifestyle, then start smoking. I still wanted to be able to run and exercise, and smoking was at direct-odds with that. So I started chewing with the intent of quitting because it's extremely unattractive, and I would do it out of respect for whoever would have to kiss me.

So I guess I walked into the habits expecting to fail at addiction, then I did. If you want to quit, you need to move the bar of what you're willing to accept. For me personally it was the ability to exercise that I wasn't willing to sacrifice, and smoking was in direct conflict of that interest, so I eliminated it. Then it was tooth decay, gum disease, and general mouth hygiene that I wasn't willing to compromise, and dipping was in direct conflict with that.

Now I'm nicotine free. I would have probably considered the e-cig option had it been available at the time, but now that I'm free I'm not going back. Oh yea, freedom from addiction is a good perk as well. Not feeling my skin crawl when I haven't had my fix in too many hours, small things that I take for granted now that seemed like big things when I was quitting.

I guess my advice is: find the reasons you want to quit that are direct conflicts-of-interest to smoking (e.g. breath easier, not stink like cigarettes all the time, save money instead of burning it), then build a lifestyle that focuses on those reasons. Make smoking an unwelcome aspect of your life, and you will get rid of it. Sorry for the BS sounding advice, but it's the best way I can put my experience abstractly.

Good luck! It's a long road, but the first two days are the hardest (physical + mental withdrawal). After that, it's pretty much just mental. Be wary of the tricky spots. For me they were at about 2 weeks e.g. "Oh, I've gone two weeks and it's not so bad, I can have a chew/smoke" - good way to backslide. Then again at about 6 months. It was probably 2 years of nicotine-free when I had a dip again, and it nearly made me vomit. So now I have that unpleasant memory (two of them, in fact, as I tried again about 1 year later to the same effect), and I can't stand the smell of cigarettes. I can clearly remember points in my life that I loved to chew and/or smoke, but now they repulse me. I don't know if that's the same for everyone, but fortunately it is for me.

Also if you backslide it's not the end of the world. I definitely did; nicotine is a powerful drug in its own right. But like I said - it was the direct conflict with lifestyle choices that I wasn't willing to sacrifice that ultimately led to me quitting for good.

Switch to e-cigarettes like sabirw said. I made the switch over 2 years ago. It was hard to switch at first, but now normal cigarettes disgust me and I can breath much better. If you're looking for a recommendation try one of these kits, and grab some liquid from here for a more budget liquid, or here for a more high end liquid.

This will give you a good overview of what goes into the liquid. A side note for the liquids, some of the flavors can be more harmful than others. I'm not sure if this is still the case, but most of the ones with butter flavoring (think butterscotch) should be avoided. If you're really worried about it you can get unflavored with 100% PG at which point you basically have an asthma inhaler with nicotine, the main difference being the liquid is heated to become a vapor instead of atomized. Also, a good rule of thumb is the darker the liquid the faster it will gum up the heating element, but they're cheap and easy to replace (~$3).

The biggest downside I've noticed is if you didn't smoke inside your house or car to avoid ruining them (ash everywhere, tar gumming things up, burn holes, lingering smell, etc.), you will probably vape in them because none of that applies anymore.

I'll second the vape thing. I have several friends that switched to e cigs. Not all of them quit, but even the ones who relapsed still cut back a ton as long as they were still using the vape. Cigs have different addictive chemicals than nicotine juice, so it might not be easy, but you don't get quite so pissed when you switch, you just crave. Quitting cold turkey from cigs takes a very determined person to stick with it, just because you feel slow and angry without them. Nicotine juice sort of isolates the psychological addiction from the physical symptoms of withdrawals, and lets you see what you're in for.

If you try it out, don't skimp on your setup. Most (if not all) disposable e-cigs are a gimmick. They're owned by the same tobacco companies that sell cigs, and have almost no nicotine. A heavy smoker will never be satisfied by one of those BS products like blu. Get online, do some research, and you can probably find a good battery and tank for ~75 bucks, and that should last you years if you don't drop the thing daily. Also make sure you buy your juice from a reputable source. I recommend buying anything vape related online, from a US based company. Gas station e juice is notorious for crazy chemicals in the flavoring that can cause health issues just as bad as cigs.
